Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; :24 adds 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row.' (2) Visual is mode="batched" (visual/judge.toml:3) and task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:12 says 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.'; :14 has the same no-double-deduction line. (3) Functional is mode="individual" (functional/judge.toml:3; comment lines 23-24 record the lead instruction), so harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 (pinned task/tests/Dockerfile:31) runs each criterion in its own agent call (_arun_agent_individual, judges.py:467-494, which calls _arun_agent_call with [c]); a per-criterion timeout zeroes only that criterion (judges.py:541-549; workspace fixture individual_timeout_retains_first keeps first=1.0 and records second=0.0). The prompt matches that structure: functional/prompt.md:9-11 '## One criterion per session ... judge it against its own bar' and :17 'Once it succeeds, carry out your criterion's steps and continue after a failed leg so the report shows every leg.' No scored prompt tells the judge to stop at first failure: a grep for stop/first fail/abort/halt/remaining/throughout/zero across the scored prompts, all judge.toml files and app_context.md finds only (a) the in-dimension global browser gate ('binary0 throughout' in polish, 'minimum raw Likert score 1' in visual), which quality-checks #29 requires in each scored prompt to zero a dead app, and (b) per-criterion self-zero clauses scoped to their own row (e.g. polish hro_pol_live_board 'If no update arrives within 60 seconds ... this row is 0'; functional hro_activity 'If no stage move succeeded in this session, this criterion is 0'). The 'Report every step' rule (functional :33, polish :22, visual :18: 'A step you skipped or did differently fails that criterion') is scoped to that criterion. NOT EXERCISED clauses (functional :35, polish :26, visual :20) zero only 'the unobserved outcome' and say 'Preserve every completed independent observation'. Gate dimensions (gates/render, gates/constraints) carry no independence wording, which is permitted (exempt). Counterexample search: a conforming app without live push fails hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread, but the polish prompt still requires scoring hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume and hro_pol_earlier_place on their own; a weakness in one visual Likert row cannot zero the others; in functional each criterion is a separate session using its own suffixed records (prompt.md:21), so one failed criterion cannot zero another. A broken/static app cannot exploit the independence wording because the in-dimension gate still zeroes it. No counterexample found. Colderwater lessons bearing on this row, checked for every instance: lesson 9 skip-fails rule (scoped per criterion in all three scored prompts); lesson 16 no double grading (polish :24 and visual :14); lesson 11 infra crash zeroing a dimension is RewardKit behaviour, not prompt wording (functional individual mode limits a timeout to one criterion; polish/visual batched sessions remain all-or-nothing on a judge timeout or CLI crash, outside this row's prompt-wording scope). Residual observations, not defects for this row: the functional prompt omits the template's literal 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure' (template functional/prompt.md:68) because each session holds exactly one criterion; the workbook Deterministic sheet scopes check-batched-independence-wording.py to batched dimensions, so the individual-mode functional prompt is outside its stated scope, but that private checker was not run here (deterministic reviewer's domain). Whether moving functional from the template's batched to individual mode is a permitted template-setting change belongs to other rows, not judged here.
